items.title: Influence-curve representers form an affine orthogonal-complement class
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space, let $\mathcal T\subseteq H$ be a closed linear subspace, and let $\dot\psi:\mathcal T\to\mathbb R^k$ be continuous linear with an ambient representer $\phi_0\in H^k$, meaning $\dot\psi(s)=\langle\phi_0,s\rangle_H$ coordinatewise for all $s\in\mathcal T$. Assume Countable Choice. Then all ambient representers are exactly

$$\phi_0+(\mathcal T^\perp)^k.$$

The unique representer in $\mathcal T^k$ is $\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\Pi_{\mathcal T}\phi_0$; when $\dot\psi$ is a statistical path derivative, this is its canonical gradient. Projection is applied coordinatewise.

items.title: Asymptotically linear estimators and influence functions
items.statement:
Fix a law $P$ and an iid sample $X_1,\ldots,X_n\sim P$. For a measurable vector function $\varphi:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^k$, write $P\varphi=E_P[\varphi(X)]$ and $P_n\varphi=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\varphi(X_i)$, where $P_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{X_i}$ is the empirical measure. For a vector remainder $R_n$, $R_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})$ means $\sqrt n R_n\to0$ in $P$-probability.

A measurable estimator sequence $\widehat\psi_n$ of $\psi(P)\in\mathbb R^k$ is **asymptotically linear at $P$** with **estimator influence function** $\varphi$ if

$$\widehat\psi_n-\psi(P)=(P_n-P)\varphi+o_P(n^{-1/2}),$$

where $\varphi\in L^2_0(P)^k$: $E_P\varphi=0$ and $E_P\|\varphi\|^2<\infty$. The space $L^2_0(P)$ and its almost-sure equivalence convention are as in [[def-mean-zero-square-integrable-space]]. This definition alone does not assert regularity under local alternatives, pathwise differentiability of $\psi$, or asymptotic normality.

items.title: Pathwise differentiability and parameter influence curves
items.statement:
Let $P$ be a probability law for one observation, let $\mathcal P$ be a model of laws containing $P$, and let $\psi:\mathcal P\to\mathbb R^k$ be a target functional, where $k\ge1$ is finite. A one-sided path $t\mapsto P_t$, $0\le t<\epsilon$, through $P=P_0$ is **differentiable in quadratic mean (DQM)** with score $s\in L^2(P)$ when its densities $p_t,p$ relative to one common sigma-finite measure $\mu$ satisfy

$$\left\|\sqrt{p_t}-\sqrt p-\frac{t}{2}s\sqrt p\right\|_{L^2(\mu)}=o(t)\qquad(t\downarrow0).$$

The score initially belongs to $L^2(P)$; [[thm-dqm-score-mean-zero]] proves it is unique modulo $P$-almost-sure equality and has mean zero, so it lies in $L^2_0(P)$ as defined by [[def-mean-zero-square-integrable-space]]. The allowed scores form the **tangent set** of the designated paths ([[def-tangent-set]]); their **tangent space** $\mathcal T$ is the closure of their real linear span in $L^2_0(P)$ ([[def-tangent-space]]). It is a closed linear subspace by [[thm-tangent-space-is-closed-linear-subspace]], and hence a Hilbert space under Countable Choice ([[thm-mean-zero-square-integrable-space-is-hilbert]]).

The functional $\psi$ is **pathwise differentiable at $P$ relative to $\mathcal T$** if the right derivative $\dot\psi_P(s):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}(\psi(P_t)-\psi(P))/t$ exists for every allowed path, depends only on its score, and extends to a continuous linear map $\dot\psi_P:\mathcal T\to\mathbb R^k$. A vector $\phi\in L^2_0(P)^k$ is a **parameter influence curve** (or representer) when

$$\dot\psi_P(s)=E_P[\phi s]\qquad(s\in\mathcal T),$$

with the expectation interpreted coordinatewise. The Hilbert-space Riesz theorem gives a unique representer in $\mathcal T^k$; it is the **canonical gradient**. This representation requires Countable Choice, as in [[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]] and [[def-countable-choice]]. The supplied density versions along a path use the separate Axiom of Choice in [[def-dqm-submodel-through-a-law]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. The full set of ambient representers and its projection characterization are proved in [[thm-influence-curve-representers]].

items.title: Efficient score and efficient information
items.statement:
Let $\theta\in\mathbb R^p$, $p\ge1$ finite, be a parameter of interest at a law $P$. Assume its score vector $S_\theta=(S_{\theta,1},\ldots,S_{\theta,p})^T$ has components in $L^2_0(P)$; under a dominated differentiable parametric submodel these are the coordinate log-density scores of [[def-score-and-fisher-information]]. Let $\mathcal T_\eta\subseteq L^2_0(P)$ be the closed nuisance tangent space of [[def-nuisance-tangent-space]]. The ambient $L^2_0(P)$ is as in [[def-mean-zero-square-integrable-space]]. The score-density convention uses the Axiom of Choice, while Hilbert projection uses Countable Choice; both dependencies are retained separately.

The Hilbert decomposition [[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]] defines $\Pi_{\mathcal T_\eta}f$ as the unique $g\in\mathcal T_\eta$ with $f-g\in\mathcal T_\eta^\perp$, where orthogonality and $\mathcal T_\eta^\perp$ have the meanings in [[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. The **efficient score vector** and **efficient information matrix** are

$$S_{\mathrm{eff}}=S_\theta-\Pi_{\mathcal T_\eta}S_\theta,\qquad I_{\mathrm{eff}}=E_P[S_{\mathrm{eff}}S_{\mathrm{eff}}^T],$$

where $\Pi_{\mathcal T_\eta}$ is the Hilbert-space orthogonal projection applied coordinatewise. This projection exists and is unique because $\mathcal T_\eta$ is a closed linear subspace; the projection theorem used by [[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]] assumes Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

items.title: Efficient score gives the canonical gradient
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $H=L^2_0(P)$, let $S_\theta\in H^p$ be a finite-dimensional interest-score vector, and let $\mathcal T_\eta\subseteq\mathcal T\subseteq H$ be closed linear nuisance and full tangent spaces, with $\mathcal T_\eta$ a subspace of $\mathcal T$. Assume the designated allowed score set is exactly

$$\mathcal S=\{a^TS_\theta+t:a\in\mathbb R^p,\ t\in\mathcal T_\eta\},\qquad \mathcal T=\overline{\mathcal S}^{\,L^2(P)},$$

and every allowed one-sided path with score $a^TS_\theta+t\in\mathcal S$ has right target derivative $a$ for the parameter $\theta$. If $I_{\mathrm{eff}}=E_P[S_{\mathrm{eff}}S_{\mathrm{eff}}^T]$ is nonsingular, then $\theta$ is pathwise differentiable and its canonical gradient is

$$\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=I_{\mathrm{eff}}^{-1}S_{\mathrm{eff}}.$$

Its covariance matrix is $E_P[\phi_{\mathrm{can}}\phi_{\mathrm{can}}^T]=I_{\mathrm{eff}}^{-1}$. This theorem does not assert that an estimator attaining the covariance bound exists.

title: Influence Functions and Efficient Scores — Examples

items.title: A mean derivative that is not continuous in the tangent norm
items.statement: Let $\Omega=\mathbb N$ with $\mathcal F=2^{\mathbb N}$, and define $X:\Omega\to[0,\infty)$ by $X(k)=k$. Let $\mathcal M_X$ be the model of probability laws $Q$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal F)$ satisfying $E_QX<\infty$, and define $\psi:\mathcal M_X\to\mathbb R$ by $\psi(Q)=E_QX$. Take $P\{X=k\}=c k^{-3}$, where $c=(\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-3})^{-1}$. Then $E_PX<\infty$ but $E_PX^2=\infty$. At $P$, designate the bounded-score one-sided paths $dP_{t,s}=(1+ts)dP$ with $E_Ps=0$ and sufficiently small $t\ge0$ as the allowed paths. Their tangent space is $L^2_0(P)$. The right derivative on bounded scores is $s\mapsto E_P[Xs]$, but this map is not continuous in the $L^2(P)$ norm. Thus $\psi$ is not pathwise differentiable relative to this tangent space and has no finite-variance influence curve there.

items.title: Mean functional and the sample-mean influence function
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ be a measurable observation space and let $X:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)$ be measurable. Let $\mathcal M_X$ be the model of probability laws $Q$ on this space satisfying $E_QX<\infty$, and define $\psi:\mathcal M_X\to\mathbb R$ by $\psi(Q)=E_QX$. Take $P\in\mathcal M_X$ with $X\in L^2(P)$, and write $\mu=E_PX$. Specify the allowed one-sided paths through $P$ to be $dP_{t,s}=(1+ts)dP$ for bounded real $s$ with $E_Ps=0$ and sufficiently small $t\ge0$. Their scores are the bounded mean-zero functions, whose closure is $\mathcal T=L^2_0(P)$. The right path derivative is represented by $X-\mu$. It is the unique representer in $\mathcal T$, hence the canonical gradient in this example. For iid observations from $P$, the sample mean has the exact expansion

$$\overline X_n-\mu=(P_n-P)(X-\mu),$$

so $X-\mu$ is also its estimator influence function. Only the specified bounded-score path class is asserted here.

items.title: A finite nuisance-score projection
items.statement:
Let $U,V$ be the coordinate functions on $\Omega=\{-1,1\}^2$, with $P$ uniform and counting measure as a common dominator. For $2|\theta|+|\eta|<1$, define
$$P_{\theta,\eta}\{(u,v)\}=\frac14\bigl(1+\theta(u+v)+\eta u\bigr).$$
Take $\theta$ as the scalar parameter of interest and $\eta$ as nuisance. At $(0,0)$ designate the straight one-sided paths $(\theta_t,\eta_t)=(at,bt)$ as allowed paths, with those having $a=0$ designated as nuisance paths. Then the interest score is $S_\theta=U+V$, the nuisance tangent space is $\mathcal T_\eta=\operatorname{span}\{U\}$, and the full tangent space is $\mathcal T=\operatorname{span}\{U,V\}$. The efficient score is $V$, the efficient information is $1$, and the canonical gradient for $\theta$ is $V$.
